step1_analysis.description: This circuit converts a control voltage (V2I) into bias voltages (BP, BN) for a voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO). It uses a replica of the VCO delay cell (including PMOS tail, PMOS inputs, and NMOS symmetric loads) to ensure the bias tracks supply variations, providing high power supply noise rejection (PSRR).

paper_reference.title: A Supply-Noise-Insensitive CMOS PLL With a Voltage Regulator Using DC–DC Capacitive Converter

dc_power.description: Total DC power consumption of the replica bias circuit at a typical control voltage.

sky130_expected.calculation: At V2I = 0.5V, I_XM10 = 0.5 * 270u * 10 * (0.5 - 0.42)^2 = 8.64 uA. The circuit has 4 main branches mirroring this current. Total current = 4 * 8.64 uA = 34.5 uA. Power = 1.8V * 34.5 uA = 62 uW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Adjusted for SKY130 1.8V supply and typical V2I operating point to keep all stacked transistors in saturation.

bp_voltage.description: DC bias voltage generated for the PMOS tail current sources of the VCO.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated based on the mirrored reference current and diode-connected PMOS square-law model.

v2i_gain.description: DC gain from the input control voltage (V2I) to the output bias voltage (BP).

sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends primarily on the ratio of NMOS to PMOS mobility and sizing, which are equal here.

psrr_vsg.description: Power supply rejection ratio of the PMOS tail source-gate voltage (VDD - BP). Measures how well the tail current is isolated from VDD noise.

sky130_expected.calculation: Since BP is generated by a diode-connected PMOS referenced to VDD, BP tracks VDD. The AC voltage across the tail (VDD - BP) should be very small. Expected AC magnitude < 0.1 V/V.
sky130_expected.reasoning: A well-designed replica bias forces the bias voltage to track the supply, yielding high rejection (highly negative dB) for the Vsg.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC operating point, V2I-to-BP gain, AC PSRR of the tail voltage, and transient response of the replica bias circuit.
